fundamental.headline: Business in a heavy investment phase, and expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 11% over the last year. Negative free cash flow because the company is investing heavily in growth (capex 48% of revenue, up from 34%); margins are improving.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 78% of the last 5 years.
drivers: Profit margins are widening: it keeps more of each sale than a year ago.
It is spending heavily on new capacity (much of it AI), faster than sales are growing; the payoff isn't proven yet.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Profits are holding up, but cash is going into new capacity and the payoff isn't proven yet: the price already assumes it works, so there's little room for disappointment. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: No rush
timing.text: Nothing urgent in the next few weeks.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 55% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (2%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 11% last year; 7%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 6% (3 years ago 5%, about the same) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $6 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 11% (3 years ago 7%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $15.9B, up 25% from a year ago — about 1.6× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $391M, up 30% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 7%/yr over 3 years and 9%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 23% vs a 5-year range of 15–23% (median 17%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $2.0B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($0M buybacks + $2.0B dividends) = 2.0% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.1% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $20.70, up 10% in 90 days (up 11% in the last 30); 6 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $18.74, up 5% in 90 days (up 5% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Americas 45% of sales, up 11%; EMEA 34% of sales, up 12%; Asia-Pacific 21% of sales, up 10%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +34% vs a year ago · $16.60 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 34% vs sales 11%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 2 quarters running, but the beats are shrinking (13% → 5%): the bar is getting harder to clear.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 11% from a year ago, about as fast as two quarters ago (10%): steady demand.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $23 of operating profit, up from $17 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Free cash flow is negative: it's spending more (often on new capacity) than the business brings in.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 61× last year's profit (its lowest in 5 years).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 10% in 90 days (6 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
